summary: A cardholder starts a billing cycle with no previous balance, makes one purchase that stays below the credit limit, receives a statement, and then pays the full statement balance before the due date. The scenario is designed to show on-time satisfaction of the minimum-payment obligation, preservation of the purchase grace period, and no late or over-limit fee outcome.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of the cycle, so the issuer's 25-day minimum grace-period obligation for new purchases is triggered.
The purchase is a standard domestic purchase, not a cash advance, balance transfer, illegal transaction, or international transaction.
The credit limit is $1000.00 and the single purchase does not exceed it, so no over-limit condition occurs.
The statement closes on 2026-05-31 and shows a new balance of $200.00; the minimum payment under the contract formula would be $15.00, but the cardholder pays the full $200.00 instead.
The payment is made through an approved standard payment channel and is credited on the date received.
Because payment is made in full on or before the due date, there is no late payment, no default for untimely payment, and no late fee.
The modeled credit-limit obligation is represented by the purchase event staying within the limit and explicitly binding to clause.4.credit_limit.
The modeled minimum-payment obligation is represented by the payment event and explicitly binding to clause.5.minimum_payment_obligation.

The modeled grace-period obligation is represented by the statement cycle providing at least 25 days from purchase to due date and explicitly bound via the statement-close event to clause.6.grace_period.
